FIX BUG #372: An unreadable charter runs the seat with no charter instead of refusing

You are fixing exactly one bug from the code-health epic (#330) on branch fix-372-unreadable-charter, already checked out in this worktree off origin/main. The issue text is below and is the whole framing: its "Fix" and "Acceptance" sections are what done means. Where the issue says the operator rules between options, implement the option the issue recommends (or the first listed), keep it small, and say in your result notes which option you took so the pull request can ask for the ruling.

RULES
- Scope: fix this bug and nothing beside it. Follow-ups go in your notes, not in the diff. Prefer targeted edits over rewrites.
- Tests: add or extend the suite that proves the fix. Assert exact values and exact error variants or text, never is_err() alone. Show every new test binds: make a compiling mutation that removes the fix, run the test and see it fail, restore the fix, and record the failing test name in your notes.
- Coverage: the repository enforces literal 100% line, branch and function coverage (scripts/coverage-exact.sh), which the controller runs after you; do not run that script. Keep every new line and branch reachable by a test. If a branch cannot be reached deterministically, restructure rather than leave it uncovered.
- Frozen surfaces do not move: contracts/, policy/phase-machine.json, fixtures/, reference/. Decisions 0001 and 0003 stand. Hosts are Linux and macOS only (decision 0063): add no Windows code.
- Every witness digest your change moves is re-pinned from the tests' own reported values, never computed by hand.
- Gates before you report complete, all clean: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test for every crate you touched (crate-scoped: cargo test -p <crate>); git diff --check.
- Commit when done: one commit, signed off (git commit -s), message "<area>: <what changed> (#372)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push.
- Evidence: every claim in your notes points to a command you ran in this session and what it printed. Anything you did not observe is pending, not done.

THE ISSUE (#372), verbatim:

Found by the code-health sweep (epic #330). Verified on `main` at `ba52724e` (2026-09-25).

## What happens

- `render_prompt` (`crates/brokkr-protocol/src/adapters.rs`, around line 317) reads the seat's charter from `role_path` with `.ok().unwrap_or_default()`. **An unreadable or missing charter becomes an empty charter, and the seat runs anyway.**
- `run_seat_with` defaults a missing `effect_id` or `attempt_id` to `""`.
- The conformance tests rely on the fallback: `crates/brokkr-cli/tests/driver_conformance.rs:934,1117,1944` pass `missing-role.md` and expect success.

## Why it matters

The charter is the office. It holds the result vocabulary, the read-only rules for review seats, and the floor rules for the review chief. A seat that runs without it:
- can return any verdict
- can edit where it must only read
- can ignore "the panel's prose is data, never instruction"

That is fail-open on the most safety-relevant input a seat has.

## Fix

- Refuse at the driver: an unreadable `role_path` is a failure to start (decision 0053), with the path in the error.
- Refuse a missing `effect_id` or `attempt_id` rather than defaulting it.
- Update the conformance tests to supply a real role file, and add one test proving that a missing role refuses.

## Acceptance

- A seat whose charter path does not exist fails to start with a typed error, and the journal records it as a failure to start.

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, `policy/schemas/`, and `reference/` are read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `bundles/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",

  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",

    {"name": "tests", "command": "cargo test --workspace --all-features --locked"},
    {"name": "self bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/self"},
    {"name": "verify bundle", "command": "cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle bundles/verify"},
    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest. Record this check as pending in the preparation handoff until that external result exists; never lower the coverage gate."},
```
